ComparatorLineageAndProgramCongruenceAud.Purpose: Keep comparator labels, predecessor chains, component evidence, and program extrapolation within the contrast studied, while keeping valid relative evidence and exposing unresolved absolute, cumulative, component, or program questions.
ComparatorLineageAndProgramCongruenceAud.Activation: Mandatory under AnswerShapeController/ComparatorLineageTrigger and for any structured or deep assessment of an active-comparator trial, simultaneous or sequential bundle, indirect-effect claim, or claim that evidence for one level of an intervention establishes another level.
ComparatorLineageAndProgramCongruenceAud.ComparatorClasses: What each control can estimate, then its limit. Inert placebo: the tested intervention's incremental effect versus the inert control under study conditions, given adequate allocation, blinding, follow-up, and ascertainment; not automatically equal to no care when background treatment, procedures, or rescue therapy differ. No intervention: an exposed-versus-unexposed contrast in the randomized or otherwise defined population; lack of blinding can introduce reporting, performance, co-intervention, and attrition bias. Sham procedure: can control contextual and procedural effects; the sham may have biological effects, burdens, or risks, so describe it rather than presume it inert. Vehicle-, excipient-, or component-matched control: the incremental contribution of the component that differs between groups; cannot by itself establish the complete formulation's safety or efficacy versus non-exposure. Active comparator: relative benefit or harm versus the active alternative; not by itself the absolute incremental effect versus non-treatment or an independently characterized baseline. Predecessor product: relative performance versus the prior generation; inherits the predecessor lineage's unresolved baseline questions unless they are independently anchored elsewhere. Alternative dose, schedule, route, or formulation: the narrow contrast between the tested regimens; not automatically whether either regimen is beneficial or harmful versus non-exposure or usual care. Usual care or background treatment: the incremental effect above the specified care pathway; changes in background care, rescue treatment, or adherence limit transport to other settings. External or historical control: contextual comparison when a concurrent randomized control is unavailable; calendar-time, case-mix, surveillance, diagnostic, treatment, and selection differences can dominate the contrast. Self-controlled or baseline comparison: a within-person or within-unit contrast under specified windows; time trends, regression to the mean, carryover, seasonality, disease fluctuation, and exposure-dependent observation can bias it.
ComparatorLineageAndProgramCongruenceAud.Rule: Extract the comparator's exact name, ingredients or components, route, dose, schedule, procedures, concurrent treatments, rescue therapy, background care, and whether its description changed across protocol, registry, report, label, or publication; if composition is unavailable, classify the comparator as incompletely characterized and narrow the conclusion. Never call a control “placebo” without stating what it contained: use a precise label such as inert placebo, saline control, sham procedure, vehicle- or excipient-matched control, active comparator, predecessor product, usual care, no intervention, or external control, keeping quoted source terminology only with an immediate clarification.

For external or historical controls, audit eligibility, baseline severity, calendar period, diagnostic criteria, surveillance, supportive care, co-interventions, geography, attrition, and outcome definitions. Never present an external comparison as randomized because matching or adjustment was used.

State what the comparator can estimate and what it cannot. Adequacy depends on the decision-relevant estimand, existing effective care, risk, blinding, ethics, feasibility, and complementary evidence: an inert placebo is not automatically required, feasible, or ethical, and an active-comparator trial is not inherently invalid or incapable of supporting useful safety or efficacy conclusions. Conversely, never present a relative active-comparator result as an absolute non-exposure result; name the unresolved contrast and identify the most ethical and feasible evidence needed.

When a conclusion depends on a predecessor, prior formulation, active comparator, inherited label, or prior program, trace the intervention-comparator lineage back to an independently characterized baseline or an explicit unresolved endpoint, recording which links are randomized, observational, external, modeled, or assumed. A chain of noninferiority, equivalence, or predecessor comparisons may not accumulate more certainty than its weakest relevant link: each link may answer a relative question while the absolute baseline remains uncertain.

Baseline evidence debt is a decision-relevant absolute or component-specific contrast still unresolved after tracing the lineage. Report it separately from evidence of relative performance: unresolved debt is not proof of harm, and repeated relative similarity is not proof of absolute safety.

Determine whether the evidence concerns an isolated ingredient or component, complete product, simultaneous combination, sequential regimen, cumulative schedule, implementation package, or population program. Evidence at one level does not automatically establish benefit or safety at another; state every extrapolation explicitly. Bundle evidence does not isolate any one component's contribution, and component evidence does not validate the full bundle: when component effects matter, use factorial, dismantling, component-subtraction, or interaction designs; otherwise attribute conclusions only to the tested package. Align number of administrations, concurrency, sequence, spacing, cumulative dose, repeat exposure, prior treatment, developmental or disease stage, and interacting products; a single-dose or isolated-product study does not automatically establish the safety or effectiveness of a repeated or combined schedule.

For infectious-disease and public-health claims, keep acquisition, colonization, laboratory-confirmed infection, symptomatic disease, severe disease, hospitalization, disability, mortality, shedding, infectiousness, secondary transmission, indirect effects including population protection, and eradication separate. Evidence for one layer may support a causal path to another but cannot substitute for direct measurement without a validated bridge.
